lesson.title: Your Forehand Leaves a Bill
lesson.hook: You run around the backhand, hit a strong forehand, then lose the exposed court.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time you run around, judge the shot and recovery as one decision.

pro.label: Courier's weapon and its bill
pro.moment: Coach Jim McLennan: Courier built his career around the inside-out and inside-in forehand, but it sometimes left him with awkward court positioning.
pro.read: Count the court your favourite shot leaves behind.

drill.name: Pay the bill
drill.how: After every run-around forehand, touch the centre mark before the next ball arrives. Miss it and you lose the point, whatever happens next.

steps.name: Wide to your backhand
steps.sit: A deep ball to your backhand. They're balanced and could go either way.
steps.q: Which shot leaves you less to cover?
opts: Run around: deep down the line
steps.payoff: The backhand leaves you closer to where their reply goes.
steps.principle: Running around costs a recovery. This ball doesn't pay it back.
steps.why: Running around takes you further from the middle. Against a balanced opponent and a deep ball, that extra distance shows up on the next shot.
steps.take: Deep ball, ready opponent? The backhand leaves less court open.

lines.A: Big forehand, but from out wide — you're stretched for their reply.
lines.B: Short across court — they step in and it's past you.
lines.C: Down the line from out wide — you're stretched for their reply.
lines.D: The backhand keeps you close to home — you're in time.

steps.name: Shorter, they're stranded
steps.sit: Now the ball is shorter. You're inside the court, and they're stranded left.
steps.q: Is running around worth it now?
opts: Run around, hit it at them
steps.payoff: Stranded opponent, shorter ball: now the forehand pays for itself.
steps.principle: Run around when the shot you get is worth the court you give.
steps.why: Hitting from inside the court shortens your way back, and they're far from the space. The same forehand that cost you on the deep ball wins here.
steps.unlock: The cost can be worth it
steps.take: Shorter ball, opponent stranded? Now the runaround forehand pays.

lines.A: Inside-out into the space — too far for them.
lines.B: To their side — they're waiting; you only just get there.
lines.C: At them — an easy reply, and you're only just in time.
lines.D: Short through the middle — they step in and it's past you.

steps.name: Deeper, wider
steps.sit: A deeper, wider ball. You're behind the baseline, and they're central again.
steps.q: Which shot gets you home in time?
opts: Run around: deep down the line
steps.payoff: Deep and wide: the high backhand buys time that running around can't.
steps.principle: When the ball takes your time, don't give away court as well.
steps.why: You're already deep and wide. Running around adds more distance; a high, deep backhand through the middle gives you time to recover.
steps.take: Deep and wide? Lift the backhand through the middle — don't pay twice.

lines.A: Down the line from out wide — you're stretched on their reply.
lines.B: High through the middle buys the time to get back.
lines.C: Short angle from deep — they step in; you're stretched.
lines.D: Deep across, but from out wide — you're stretched on their reply.
